The [starter](../../starters/zephyr-native-sim.md) made a west workspace
pinned to Zephyr 3.7, scaffolded a talker for `board = "zephyr"`, and ran it
on `native_sim`, Zephyr's host build, where the image is a Linux executable.
This page covers what comes after it: where an image's nano-ros and Zephyr
settings each go, the Zephyr lines nano-ros builds against, what is particular
to `native_sim`, and how `nros build` hands the build to `west`. The
configuration here applies to every Zephyr board; the
[mps2-an385](zephyr.md) and [Nucleo-F767ZI](nucleo-f767zi.md) pages add
only their board notes.

## Configure the platform

An image's nano-ros configuration lives in one place, the bringup's
`system.toml`. Zephyr's own settings (networking, POSIX, stacks, heaps) live
in Zephyr's `prj.conf` fragments, which the image names with `os_config`:

```toml
[system]
name = "zs_node"
rmw = "zenoh"
domain_id = 0

[image.zephyr]
# a nano-ros board id; west gets native_sim/native/64
board = "zephyr"
locator = "tcp/127.0.0.1:7447"
os_config = ["prj-zenoh.conf"]    # Zephyr settings only

[image.zephyr.knobs.zenoh]
max_publishers = 4
```

nano-ros's Zephyr module renders the image into a Kconfig fragment and
merges it last, after every conf file. So a `prj*.conf` file holds Zephyr's
settings only, and never a `CONFIG_NROS_*` line: one there is either
overridden or a second source that can disagree with the first.

| You write in `system.toml` | The build gets |
| --- | --- |
| `rmw = "xrce"` | `CONFIG_NROS_RMW_XRCE=y` |
| (the node package's language) | `CONFIG_NROS_{C,CPP,RUST}_API=y` |
| `locator = "tcp/…"` (zenoh) | `CONFIG_NROS_ZENOH_LOCATOR` |
| `locator = "udp/<host>:<port>"` (XRCE) | `CONFIG_NROS_XRCE_AGENT_ADDR` and `_PORT` |
| `domain_id = 7` | `CONFIG_NROS_DOMAIN_ID` |
| `[image.<id>.knobs.zenoh] max_queryables = 12` | `CONFIG_NROS_MAX_QUERYABLES=12` |
| `env = { NROS_ZEPHYR_TASK_STACK_SIZE = "16384" }` | `CONFIG_NROS_ZEPHYR_TASK_STACK_SIZE=16384` |
| `os_config = ["prj-xrce.conf"]` | that fragment, ahead of your own `EXTRA_CONF_FILE` |

A key whose value does not fit its Kconfig symbol, or that exists only under
another RMW, is refused when the build configures, naming the
`system.toml` line. [Configure an image](../build/configure-an-image.md)
lists the knobs.

### One image per RMW

A bringup built for several backends states one image per RMW and picks one
at build time. The copy-out C talker,
[`examples/zephyr/c/talker/src/nros_zephyr_talker_c_bringup/system.toml`](https://github.com/NEWSLabNTU/nano-ros/blob/main/examples/zephyr/c/talker/src/nros_zephyr_talker_c_bringup/system.toml),
does this:

```toml
[system]
name = "nros_zephyr_talker_c"
rmw = "zenoh"
domain_id = 0
default_images = ["zephyr_zenoh"]

[image.zephyr_zenoh]
board = "zephyr"
rmw = "zenoh"
os_config = ["prj-zenoh.conf", "prj-zenoh-native-sim.conf"]

[image.zephyr_xrce]
board = "zephyr"
rmw = "xrce"
os_config = ["prj-xrce.conf"]
locator = "udp/127.0.0.1:2018"
```

`nros build` builds the `default_images`, and `nros build zephyr_xrce`
builds the other. Each image has its own build directory,
`build/<platform>-<rmw>/<package>__<image>_west`, so switching never reuses
another image's cache.

What each backend needs from Zephyr goes in its fragment:

- **zenoh:** TCP and POSIX threads, with pthread pools big enough for
  zenoh-pico (`CONFIG_MAX_PTHREAD_MUTEX_COUNT=64`,
  `CONFIG_MAX_PTHREAD_COND_COUNT=16`).
- **XRCE-DDS:** `CONFIG_NET_TCP=y`, on the BSD sockets every image enables.
- **Cyclone DDS:** `CONFIG_CPP=y` (its source is C++, even for a Rust node),
  `CONFIG_MAIN_STACK_SIZE=524288`, and `CONFIG_NET_IPV4_IGMP=y` for
  discovery. Raise its heap with `[image.<id>.knobs.zephyr] heap_size`, not
  in the conf.

## The Zephyr lines

nano-ros builds as a module against whichever Zephyr your west workspace
pins: the 3.7 LTS line (the starters' pin) or the 4.x line. The two differ in
two places:

- **Python.** 3.7 needs Python 3.10 or later; 4.x needs 3.12 or later. On a
  host with an older Python, make a 3.12 virtual environment and run `west`
  from it.
- **An app with no `system.toml`.** On 4.x, nano-ros's `west` snippets pick
  the RMW on the build line, `west build -S nros-cyclonedds …`. With a
  `system.toml`, the image's `rmw` decides on both lines, and a snippet that
  names a different RMW is refused.

## Board notes

- **`board = "zephyr"` is `native_sim/native/64`.** The board's descriptor
  states the id `west build -b` receives, so an image never names it.
- **Sockets are the host's.** The board applies nano-ros's `nros-nsos`
  snippet, which routes the image's sockets through Zephyr's NSOS offload to
  the host kernel. The image reaches a router on loopback with no TAP
  interface and no root access. Without the snippet, `native_sim` tries to
  create one and fails with `eth_posix: Cannot create zeth`.
- **nano-ros patches Zephyr's NSOS driver** (`recvmsg`, IPv4 multicast).
  `nros setup zephyr` applies the patches to your workspace, checked by
  hash. After a `west update` resets the tree, run the same command again to
  reapply them.
- **The console is standard output,** and the image runs until you stop it.

## Read the run plan

From the starter's workspace, print the plan `nros run` follows:

```bash probe=410
nros run zs_node --dry-run --why
```

The target is a host process: `nros run` runs the built `zephyr.exe`, and the
console is its standard output. A zenoh image's link is the image's
`locator`, and `nros run` starts the router the link needs.

## Drive west yourself

On Zephyr, `nros build` writes a Zephyr application for the image under
`build/`, then runs `west build` on it from your west workspace with the
image's overlays applied (`EXTRA_CONF_FILE`, `EXTRA_DTC_OVERLAY_FILE`,
`APPLICATION_CONFIG_DIR`). Print that `west build` line without running it:

```bash probe=420
nros build --dry-run
```

Copy the line to run west yourself. Anything after `--` on the
`nros build` line goes to west, to its option zone or its CMake zone by
west's own flag list, so `nros build -- -p always -DMY_OPT=1` reaches both.
Two flags are refused, because the image decides them: `-b`, which comes
from the image's `board`, and `--sysbuild`, which comes from a
`sysbuild.conf` beside the application.

`nros build` finds your Zephyr through `--zephyr-workspace <dir>`,
`$ZEPHYR_BASE` or `$NROS_ZEPHYR_WORKSPACE` (the starter exported the last).
When it finds none it stops and prints the `west build` line and where to run
it, rather than guess. nano-ros never writes into the west workspace.

When a change needs the application's own `CMakeLists.txt` or `prj.conf`,
take the application over with `nros materialize zephyr`. That writes it to
`src/zephyr_entry/`, and `nros build` builds your copy from then on. Delete
the directory to return to the generated one. An application that owns its
`west build` and has no bringup at all is
[A Zephyr app you build with west](zephyr-west-app.md).

## If it doesn't work

- **`<err> … executor open failed: Transport(ConnectionFailed)`:** the
  image found no router. Both sides default to `tcp/127.0.0.1:7447`; a
  `locator` changed on one side must change on the other.
- **`Could NOT find Python3 … required is at least "3.12"`:** a 4.x
  workspace on an older Python. Run `west` from a 3.12 environment.
- **`undefined symbol ETH_NATIVE_POSIX`:** 4.x renamed it `ETH_NATIVE_TAP`;
  the board's NSOS fragment handles it, so a conf file of your own should
  not set it.
- **Everything else:** [Troubleshoot](../deploy/troubleshoot.md).
